title: orchestrator-session-ledger/0
description: DRAFT (promotion-receipt/v0 draft_revision 2). NOT a separate contract directory: the shape a wrapper-written session ledger takes when promotion-receipt/v0's evaluateReceipt() consumes it. One ledger per promotion_id (the storage unit). Each entry records that the orchestrator wrapper itself launched a review session (session_id, started_at, args_digest) and that the session produced exactly the review-findings/v1 record whose WHOLE-record JCS sha256 is review_record_digest, carrying independence_code. What this proves is technical execution separation ONLY -- never human or organizational independence. Semantic MUSTs enforced by checkSessionLedger() in evaluate.mjs: started_at is a real UTC date; review_record_digest is unique within the ledger (one record has at most one entry); one session_id never appears with two different (started_at, args_digest) pairs; entries are sorted strictly ascending by review_record_digest (so the ledger's JCS digest is a canonical representation -- entry order carries no meaning beyond that). An unsupported ledger_version fails the const below and is rejected, never treated as 'ledger unavailable'.

review_record_digest.description: JCS (RFC 8785) sha256 of the WHOLE review-findings/v1 record this session produced -- the same record_digest promotion-receipt evidence_refs[].digest binds.
